main_wing_spar.name: Tapered I-beam main spar
main_wing_spar.model: Timoshenko beam FEA, 2 DOF/node, 21 sizing stations + Saint-Venant root-warping stress recovery
assumptions: Same solver and stations as the contract FeaResult; optimisation scales t_f and t_w linearly root→tip
Gauges clamped to Raymer minimums t_f ≥ 2.0 mm, t_w ≥ 1.5 mm
Mass is one semi-span of spar (multiply by 2 for both wings)
main_wing_spar.convergence_note: Stations fixed by the spar sizing (21 nodes).

metrics.governing: outer cap fibre at y = 0.55 m

ai_proposal.rationale: The baseline margin of 0.1094 is governed by outer cap bending near the root at y = 0.55 m, while mid-to-tip stresses are elevated up to station 8. Slightly trimming tip gauge sheds outboard mass while keeping the interpolated gauge at y = 0.55 m and mid-span above the 0.10 margin threshold.

verified_metrics.governing: outer cap fibre at y = 0.55 m

ai_proposal.verdict: accepted: solver confirms the constraint and a near-optimal objective

ai_proposal.rationale: Transferring mass from the lightly loaded outboard tip into the root cap and web reduces peak bending stress at the governing y = 0.55 m station. The larger tip gauge reduction offsets the heavier root section to keep total mass below baseline.

wing_skin_box.name: NACA 2415 wing torsion box
wing_skin_box.model: NACA 2415 single-cell thin-wall box: Timoshenko bending + Bredt-Batho torsion, 25 nodes
assumptions: Bending, shear and span loads are the wing's Schrenk loads from the preliminary sizing
Skin carries the full ultimate wing bending (spar caps excluded: conservative, no stringers)
Torque t(y) = q·c·(0.10 − 0.05/1.2): lift at c/4, box reference at 0.35c, c_m0 = −0.05 at c_l ≈ 1.2
Spar webs at 15% and 60% chord; 10 ribs per side, 0.8 mm, 50% lightening holes
Uniform-gauge baseline from a first-pass hand sizing to margin +0.25; skin buckling not checked
wing_skin_box.convergence_note: Peak σ_vM re-solved at three node counts.

metrics.governing: skin (bending + Bredt torsion) at y = 0.00 m

ai_proposal.rationale: With a generous 0.25 baseline margin at the root skin and rapidly decaying stress toward the tip, aggressive tip thinning to the 0.60 lower bound and a reduction at the root safely bring the peak combined bending and Bredt-Batho shear stress near the 0.10 margin limit.

fuselage_frames.name: Carry-through ring frames and bridge
fuselage_frames.model: Closed-ring force method (2 redundants, 721 points/half ring) + carry-through beam
assumptions: Fuselage radius 0.64 m scaled from a 1.22 m GA cabin by MTOW^(1/3) (assumed)
Wing root shear split 70% main / 15% front / 15% rear frame; reacted by skin shear q = 2V·sinφ/(πR)
Bridge = spar root I-section carrying the full root moment across the cabin
Frames are 65 mm deep I-sections; uniform-gauge baseline from hand sizing to margin +0.25
fuselage_frames.convergence_note: Frame peak (excluding the bridge) vs ring integration points per half ring.

metrics.governing: carry-through bridge cap (root moment)

ai_proposal.rationale: The carry-through bridge cap is right at the margin limit (0.1024), so the main frame and bridge gauge must remain at 1.0. However, the front and rear ring frames peak at only 208 MPa and can be thinned to 0.65 to save substantial mass.
ai_proposal.verdict: accepted: solver confirms the constraint and a near-optimal objective

ai_proposal.rationale: Combining a 0.72 gauge reduction on the secondary front and rear frames with the 1.05x mass budget allows a 1.26 gauge multiplier on the main carry-through bridge, substantially dropping peak root cap bending stress.

engine_mount.name: Engine mount spaceframe truss
engine_mount.model: Pin-jointed 3D spaceframe: direct stiffness (24 DOF, 14 bars) + Euler buckling per member
assumptions: Engine + propeller mass 0.11 × MTOW at 0.30 m ahead of the ring, inertia n_ult·m·g (assumed)
Ultimate thrust 1.5 × 0.25 × MTOW·g; propeller torque and gyroscopic loads not modelled
Firewall hard points pinned; members pinned-pinned (K = 1) for buckling
Zone factor k scales tube OD and wall by √k (constant D/t); baseline hand-sized to margin +0.25
engine_mount.convergence_note: Exact for a pin-jointed truss (one bar element per member).

metrics.governing: member D4 (buckling)

ai_proposal.rationale: The baseline 0.25 margin is governed by Euler buckling in diagonal member D4 (tip zone), whereas the longeron tubes (root zone) carry at most 130 MPa against a 338 MPa allowable. Aggressively downsizing the longerons to 0.65 and slightly trimming the diagonals to 0.95 minimizes mass while keeping D4 buckling margin above 0.10.
ai_proposal.verdict: rejected by solver: margin -0.36, mass 1.02 kg breaks the goal constraint

metrics.governing: member L3 (buckling)
member L3 (buckling)

min_mass.rationale: Grid search over 169 solver runs; lightest gauge set holding margin ≥ +0.10. Longeron tubes ×0.90, diagonal & ring tubes ×1.00: mass -0.03 kg, peak σ_vM 130 → 145 MPa, margin +0.25 → +0.21. Governing: member L3 (buckling).

ai_proposal.rationale: Because Euler buckling in diagonal D4 governs the mount margin and scales quadratically with tube dimensions (linearly with k), shifting mass from the axial-stress-governed longerons (k_root = 0.75) into the diagonal and ring tubes (k_tip = 1.15) boosts the overall buckling margin within baseline mass.
ai_proposal.verdict: rejected by solver: margin -0.16, mass 1.22 kg breaks the goal constraint

ai_proposal.rationale: To minimize peak axial and bending von Mises stress in the root longeron tubes, k_root is increased to 1.45 while the diagonal and ring tubes are slightly trimmed to 0.95 to maintain a safe D4 buckling margin and stay under 1.05x baseline mass.
